Detachments

Crusher Stampede · 2 DP · Purge the Foe

Enraged Behemoths

TYRANIDS MONSTER models get +1 to hit once their unit is below Starting Strength, and +1 to wound as well once it's Below Half-strength. Monster units at Starting Strength (and not Battle-shocked) get +2 OC per model.

On a single monster, the first wound flips it from "+2 OC" to "+1 to hit". The +1 cancels the −1 from Damaged.

Talons of the Norn Queen · 1 DP · Take and Hold

Higher Imperatives

Each Norn gets Protean Purpose: once per battle, in your Command phase, it can re-pick its Singular Purpose (an enemy unit to re-roll hits and wounds against, or an objective for OC 15 and FNP 5+ while in range).

Brings Lesser Prey, Tanglestrike Rounds, Catalytic Biofortification, and the Synaptoprescience upgrade.

Army rules

Synapse · Shadow in the Warp

Synapse: TYRANIDS units within 6" of a SYNAPSE model test Battle-shock on 3D6 and get +1 S in melee.

Shadow in the Warp: once per battle in either Command phase, every enemy unit tests Battle-shock, at −1 if within 6" of your SYNAPSE units.

Range and tempo

Charges

Engagement range is 2", so a charge needs a 2D6 roll of gap − 2. You can only declare against units within 12".

Unit abilities that matter

  • Onslaught (Hive Tyrant aura 6"): friendly ranged weapons get [ASSAULT] and [LETHAL HITS]. Your Exocrines can Advance and still shoot.
  • Will of the Hive Mind (Hive Tyrant): once per battle round, −1 CP on a stratagem used on a unit within 12".
  • Guardian Organism: the Tyrant has FNP 5+ while leading the Guard.
  • Encephalic Diffusion (Maleceptor aura 6"): enemies within 6" get −1 to hit, and −1 to wound too when Below Half.
  • Symbiotic Targeting (Exocrine): after it shoots, one unit it hit is hit-re-rolled on 1s by the rest of your army this phase. Shoot Exocrines first.
  • Singular Purpose / Harpoon Barbs / Harpooned (Norns): see the Norn playbook.
  • Resilient Organism (Tyrannofex): once per battle, set one attack's Damage to 0. Save it for a lascannon or melta.
  • Disruption Bombardment (Barbgaunts): one INFANTRY unit they hit gets −2" M and −2 to Advance and charge rolls.
  • Unnatural Resistance (Emissary): FNP 4+ against mortal wounds.

Game plan

Strengths

  • Ten monster units at T10–12, most with 2+ saves or 4+ invulns. Small arms barely scratch you.
  • 77 OC at full strength. The Assimilator alone holds a Singular Purpose objective at OC 15.
  • Serious long-range anti-tank (rupture cannon, harpoon, neurolance) plus five blast weapons for elites.
  • Five SYNAPSE units: everything sits in Synapse almost by default.
  • Two Maleceptors make the centre a −1 to hit zone.

Weaknesses

  • Only 11 units, and just one cheap one (Barbgaunts) for actions and secondary errands.
  • The +2 OC disappears on the first wound. A chip-damaged army has only 51 OC.
  • Armies with lots of Lethal Hits, Devastating Wounds or mortal wounds trade well into big single models.
  • No Deep Strike, no Scouts, nothing fast. The Tyrant brick walks at 6".
  • Exocrines and Maleceptors lose accuracy at 5 wounds or less.

Rules of thumb

  1. Pick Singular Purpose at the start of round 1. Assimilator takes the objective it will sit on (usually centre). Emissary takes the enemy unit that threatens you most.
  2. The rupture Tyrannofex stays on your home objective all game. It needs to move 3" or less to keep the Heavy +1, and it is your 48" fire lane.
  3. Keep the Exocrines inside the Hive Tyrant's 6" Onslaught bubble: Lethal Hits on 5 blast cannons, and they can Advance and still shoot.
  4. Shoot an Exocrine first each turn, then use Symbiotic Targeting so everyone else re-rolls 1s to hit that unit.
  5. Use Will of the Hive Mind every round. A 1 CP stratagem on a unit near the Tyrant is free.
  6. Hold Shadow in the Warp for the Command phase when two or three enemy units on objectives sit within 6" of a Maleceptor or Norn.
  7. Send Barbgaunts on Cleanse, Plunder or Burden of Trust errands so the monsters stay on the primary.

Norn playbook

280 pts · M10 · T11 · 2+ / 4++ · 16 W

Norn Assimilator

  • Purpose: objective. Pick the centre (or the contested expansion). While in range it has OC 15 and FNP 5+. With a 4++ it is the hardest piece in the list to remove.
  • Harpoon first, then charge. Hitting a MONSTER/VEHICLE with the harpoon gives +2 to the charge roll, but it must end engaged with that unit.
  • Lesser Prey makes its talons S12 (with Synapse) and its harpoon S15. Use it on T10+ targets.
  • Harpoon Barbs: enemies falling back from it take D6 mortal wounds on a 2+. That makes it a sticky tarpit for vehicles.
  • Protean Purpose: when the objective is safe late in the game, re-point it at the unit you must kill.
250 pts · M10 · T11 · 2+ / 4++ · 16 W

Norn Emissary

  • Purpose: enemy unit. Re-rolling hits and wounds on its best target is worth more than a second OC 15 anchor.
  • Tendril profiles: neurolance (Melta 2) for vehicles, neuroblast (2D6 blast) for infantry, neuroparasite (Precision) to snipe characters.
  • Melee: talons plus rending claws as extra attacks. 10 attacks at WS 2+, so Lesser Prey is rarely needed.
  • FNP 4+ against mortal wounds makes it the right body to send at psykers and Devastating Wounds units.
  • Protean Purpose: re-target once its first prey is dead.

You start low on CP and gain 1 per Command phase. Will of the Hive Mind takes 1 CP off one stratagem per round on a unit within 12" of the Tyrant.

Secondaries

From the 2026–27 Chapter Approved deck: two cards drawn each Command phase, with one 1 CP swap per battle.

Keep
  • Secure No Man's Land: two NML objectives is your default state.
  • Bring It Down: rupture cannon, harpoon and neurolance exist for this.
  • A Tempting Target: send a 7 OC monster.
  • Defend Stronghold (from round 2): rupture Tyrannofex sits on home.
  • Overwhelming Force: you fight on objectives anyway.
  • Centre Ground: the Assimilator parks there.
Usually keep
  • No Prisoners: good against MSU, slow against elite armies.
  • Assassination: neuroparasite Precision helps.
  • A Grievous Blow: only against hordes of 13+ models.
  • Cleanse: Barbgaunts plus one monster that skips shooting.
  • Burden of Trust: easy with OC 7 bodies, but it pins them.
  • Forward Position: if their home is already falling.
  • Beacon: a Norn walking out of your territory scores 5.
Discard
  • Behind Enemy Lines: nothing fast or deep-striking.
  • Outflank: drags monsters to table edges.
  • Engage on All Fronts: 11 units, mostly slow.
  • Display of Might: you'll rarely out-count them in NML.
  • Plunder: costs a shooting phase in their half.

Matchup

No opponent given, so this is the general read. Send me their list and I'll add their real units to the tables.

Target order

  1. Their anti-monster guns: lascannons, meltas, Devastating Wounds and Lethal Hits units. Rupture cannon and neurolance first.
  2. Their fastest objective units and action monkeys. Exocrines and acid spray.
  3. Screens sitting on No Man's Land objectives. Acid spray, neuroblast, Barbgaunts.
  4. Characters, when Assassination is live. Neuroparasite.

What beats this list

  • Massed anti-tank that kills a 16 W monster per turn. Lead with the Maleceptor −1 to hit aura, and keep 1 CP for Savage Roar.
  • Mortal-wound spam (psychic, Devastating Wounds). Send the Emissary, and keep Catalytic Biofortification for the Assimilator.
  • Cheap OC-heavy hordes plus actions. You win the fight but can lose the secondaries race with 11 units.
  • Deep strike onto your home: the rupture Tyrannofex denies 8" around itself just by standing there. Don't move it.
Against Purge the Foe, they score for kills. Hand them single-model monsters slowly: keep Damaged units behind ruins and trade forward with full-health ones.
